transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks now. I just feel completely flat, and even my usual hobbies don't interest me at all.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt this same way, or is this the very first time you are experiencing these feelings?

No, this isn't the first time. I've actually had these big swings between feeling really revved-up and then falling into these long, heavy downturns off and on for several years now. This current low period has been dragging on for about six months.
During those "revved-up" periods, did your energy and mood ever get so intense that it caused major problems in your life, or even required hospitalization?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized or had my life fall apart during those times. In fact, my managers actually praised my initiative and high output during those high-energy stretches, even though I was sleeping very little and snapping at my husband and coworkers. Looking back, it felt way out of proportion, but it didn't cause any major disasters.
During these low periods, have you ever experienced severe symptoms like thoughts of ending your life, or found yourself completely unable to function at work or home?

On the rougher nights, I do lie in bed thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I didn't wake up, and I've even idly wondered how to make it look like an accident, though I've never acted on it. I'm not completely paralyzed, but my work performance has definitely slipped, I've missed deadlines, and I'm bailing on chores and social plans so much that my husband is picking up most of the slack.
Between these high and low periods, do you have times when your mood feels completely normal and stable, and if so, how long do those stable periods typically last?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It feels like I'm almost always either in a revved-up phase or a heavy low phase, and I can't really recall having any long periods of feeling completely normal or stable in between.
During these low periods, do you also experience other symptoms like major changes in your appetite or sleep, constant fatigue, or difficulty concentrating?

Yes, I feel constantly wiped out no matter how much I sleep, and my concentration is shot—even simple things like comparing data or deciding what to eat feel completely overwhelming because my brain won't settle. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite, though.
When you have those "revved-up" periods, how long do they typically last? Do they usually go on for at least four days in a row, or are they shorter than that?

Oh, they definitely last much longer than four days. Those revved-up periods usually go on for weeks or even months at a time, like the high-energy phase I had during our product relaunch. I've experienced those multi-week swings off and on for several years now.
During these low periods, do you often experience strong feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or find yourself constantly blaming yourself for things?

Yes, I feel that way almost constantly. I feel like I'm screwing everything up, letting my team down because I couldn't keep up my previous pace, and being a total burden to my husband because I'm so checked out. I even catch myself thinking that I don't actually deserve any of the praise or promotions I've received.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a history of recurrent mood swings consisting of hypomanic episodes (periods of increased energy, high output, irritability, and decreased need for sleep lasting weeks to months without causing severe impairment or requiring hospitalization) and depressive episodes (current episode lasting six months characterized by flat mood, anhedonia, fatigue, poor concentration, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, and passive suicidal ideation). This clinical picture of alternating hypomanic and depressive episodes meets the criteria for Bipolar Affective Disorder (F31).
